title: oh.war/sas-revision/v1
description: Hand-written and normative for the frozen record `oh.war/sas-revision/v1` (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md): one revision of the SAS, `docs/sas/revisions/<version>.toml`, read as TOML into this JSON object. It pins a version of the specification to the sha256 of its bytes, carries section 106 as it stood, and moves from `proposed` to `accepted` once, by a human. Where this schema and the prose that governs the record (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, SAS section 101) disagree, the prose wins and this schema is the defect. Not expressed here: that `sha256` is the digest of `source`'s bytes, that `predecessor` names an existing revision, that a revision drops no requirement id of its predecessor (section 34.1), and that an accepted revision never changes.
$comment: Written from crates/openwarrant-core/src/sas.rs: SAS_REVISION_SCHEMA at sas.rs:34, `SasRevision` at sas.rs:106, `SasAcceptance` at sas.rs:93, `SasRevision::validate` at sas.rs:151 and `check_acceptance` at sas.rs:175. `actor_kind` is crates/openwarrant-core/src/contract.rs:81 `ActorKind` under `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`, so the third variant is spelled `policyservice` on the wire even though its Display is `policy_service`. The struct has no deny_unknown_fields, so the reader ignores a member it does not know; this schema refuses one, because a frozen record gains a member only when its schema does (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, Additive only). sas.rs is pinned by resolved OW-WAR-0062, which is why `war schemas` does not generate this schema.

version.description: The SAS version this revision pins (`1.3.0`, `0.1.0-draft.3`).

sha256.description: sha256 of the document's exact bytes: 64 hex digits, no prefix.

requirements.description: Section 106 as it stood in this revision: requirement id to requirement text.

architecture_changing.description: Section 101.3: decided at proposal from the section 106 diff against the predecessor. `false` when absent.

allOf.description: sas.rs:158: an accepted revision carries its acceptance.
sas.rs:192: an architecture-changing revision is accepted with an ADR reference (section 101.3).

actor_kind.description: sas.rs:181: an agent never accepts a SAS revision (section 27.2).

effective_time.description: When the acceptance took effect. Every recorded revision writes an RFC 3339 UTC time; the reader admits any string.

adr_ref.description: Required when the revision is architecture-changing.
